hypothesis_summary: The module `system_logic/generate_agent_index.py` exhibits high Cognitive Complexity, particularly in the `parse_profile` and `extract_markdown_table_data` functions (CCR001 violations). The monolithic structure of `parse_profile` handles multiple parsing strategies (YAML, Markdown tables, regex fallbacks) sequentially within a single execution block, violating the Single Responsibility Principle and complicating control flow. Hypothesis: Decomposing `parse_profile` into separate, focused strategy functions (e.g., `_apply_yaml_data`, `_apply_table_data`, `_apply_regex_heuristics`) and orchestrating them via simple delegation will reduce the peak cognitive complexity below the threshold (10), enhancing maintainability and align with the Generative Ratchet principle.
justification_or_plan: 1. Run pytest to establish baseline. 2. Write a comprehensive refactoring script (`refactor_index.py`) that uses string replacement to rewrite the overly complex functions (`parse_profile` and helpers) into modular sub-functions. 3. Run the script. 4. Run `flake8` to fix formatting (E501, E302, etc.) using `autopep8`. 5. Re-run `radon cc -a system_logic/generate_agent_index.py` and `flake8 --max-cognitive-complexity=10 system_logic/generate_agent_index.py` to verify the fix. 6. Run `pytest` to verify behavior.
